answer: Keep one hollow log hive per agent on a named ridge crest, its queen marked with a quill dipped in a dye mixed only for that hive. Each week the keeper weighs the hive at noon, with the sun at its zenith and the foragers out, and posts the weight on a public board. A traveling inspector re-weighs one hive in ten each month and checks the dye mark on the queen; a hive with a dead queen or an off-season weight loses its ridge for a year. A thousand fake names need a thousand live hives, a thousand marked queens, and a thousand weekly climbs to weigh them.
